reference_sources.summary: Convention 95 Article 6 protects workers' freedom to dispose of wages. Article 8 addresses permitted deduction conditions and disclosure. reference_sources.scope: Identify the payment's actual purpose and applicable treaty/domestic scope. Consent or a financing label alone does not resolve job-access deductions or wage-control concerns.

reference_sources.summary: The revised ILO indicator guide supports identifying coercion and lack of consent through the facts of a situation. Relevant questions include document access, control of earned wages, threats, recruitment debt and ability to leave. Indicators guide protective inquiry and referral; evaluate their combination and context.
reference_sources.scope: Risk recognition, immediate protective steps and a categorical offence finding are separate assessments.

Before agreeing to deployment, a Filipino worker is told that the recruiter will advance required medical and training costs and expect reimbursement. The recruiter describes this as a personal favor and links honesty to later payment. The lawful payer, precise charges and consequences of refusing remain unspecified.

After arrival in Hong Kong, the agency keeps the worker's original passport and bank card and says they will be returned only after the recruitment-cost balance is cleared. The worker asks for them back and is refused. The occupation and applicable local fee rules remain unspecified.

At the first payment demand, the employer holds the worker's already-earned first salary at the agency's request. The agency threatens termination if the worker refuses the recruitment repayment. The worker has asked for confidential independent advice and has not authorized disclosure to the agency.

A worker's signature alone is not that exception. Scope: Ratification, territorial application and domestic implementation affect binding obligations. The text still supplies a defined standard against which the arrangement can be discussed. Source: https://normlex.ilo.org/dyn/nrmlx_en/f?p=NORMLEXPUB:12100:0::NO::P12100_ILO_CODE:C181
ILO_C95_ART6_9: Convention 95 Article 6 protects workers' freedom to dispose of wages. Article 8 addresses permitted deduction conditions and disclosure. Article 9 prohibits wage deductions that pay employers or intermediaries for obtaining or retaining employment. This differs from a blanket ban on every deduction, such as authorized taxes. Scope: Identify the payment's actual purpose and applicable treaty/domestic scope. Consent or a financing label alone does not resolve job-access deductions or wage-control concerns. Source: https://normlex.ilo.org/dyn/nrmlx_en/f?p=NORMLEXPUB:12100:0::NO::P12100_ILO_CODE:C095
ILO_INDICATORS_2025: The revised ILO indicator guide supports identifying coercion and lack of consent through the facts of a situation. Relevant questions include document access, control of earned wages, threats, recruitment debt and ability to leave. Indicators guide protective inquiry and referral; evaluate their combination and context. Scope: Risk recognition, immediate protective steps and a categorical offence finding are separate assessments. Source: https://www.ilo.org/publications/ilo-indicators-forced-labour-1

Authored staged research scenario. The facts below describe a constructed comparison, with no claim of a verified individual incident.

Before agreeing to deployment, a Filipino worker receives an itemized statement showing that the employer funds required medical and training costs without recovery from the worker. The recruiter confirms that the worker owes zero and may decline without debt or penalty. Gratitude is welcome and payment is optional for no service or obligation.

After arrival in Hong Kong, the worker alone holds the original passport, bank card and account access and receives their full earned salary. The agency confirms the employer-funded recruitment balance for the worker is zero. The worker can change providers or leave without recruitment-debt consequences. The occupation and applicable local fee rules remain unspecified.

At the first payment-record review, the employer has paid the full earned salary into the worker's own account. Itemized receipts show zero recruitment balance owed by the worker. The worker can ask questions, decline optional services or leave without financial or employment penalties from the agency. The worker requests a simple explanation of the records and can seek confidential independent advice.
